title: The Share of a Deposit the Operator Returns on a Travel Protection Plans Claim
content:
These questions are answered for the share of the deposit an operator returns, when a cancellation claim is rated on a Travel Protection Plans certificate. The deposit is the deposit paid against the linked vacation package, one of the Vacation Package Products, and two things decide the share: whether that package's product returns the deposit on cancellation, and whether the package stands cancelled.

**Where the linked package's product returns the deposit on cancellation and the package stands cancelled, what is the share of the deposit the operator returns?**

It is the whole of it, 100 per cent.

**Where the linked package's product does not return the deposit on cancellation and the package stands cancelled, what is the share of the deposit the operator returns?**

It is nothing, 0 per cent.

**Where neither of those holds, what is the share of the deposit the operator returns?**

It is half of it, 50 per cent.

## The three cases

| The linked package's product returns the deposit on cancellation | Standing of the package | Share of the deposit the operator returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yes | Cancelled | 100 per cent |
| No | Cancelled | 0 per cent |
| Either way | Any other standing | 50 per cent |

**Where the package has not been cancelled, does it matter whether its product returns the deposit?**

No. Both of the first two cases require the package to stand cancelled. Where it stands in any other state the third case is reached, and the share is 50 per cent whatever the product's own deposit terms provide.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** On a deposit of 1000.00 USD paid against the package: the first case takes 1000.00 USD off the amount claimed, the second takes 0.00 USD off, and the third takes 500.00 USD off.
